topic: SI Base Units and Derived Units
title: Who Set the Metre? SI Units Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Two cooks in two cities both use one kilogram of rice, and every watch counts the same second. They never met, so how do they agree? Aarav finds out the hard way when a 13 mm spanner slips on a half inch bolt. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we meet the International System of Units (SI): its seven base units and the derived units built from them.

A live simulation shows a light pulse crossing one metre in about 3.34 nanoseconds, with a readout and an x-t graph whose slope is the speed of light, because today the metre is defined by fixing c = 299 792 458 m/s. We see how the second (caesium-133) and the kilogram (Planck constant, since 2019) are tied to fixed numbers of nature, build the joule step by step (1 J = 1 kg m^2 s^-2), open up the newton, pascal and watt, and learn the SI rules for writing unit names and symbols. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example, the exam trap about the gram, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
